correctness.rationale: The complete pair-distance forms prove the only possible diameters. For even n the two extreme-distance edge classes form an even cycle and opposite chords at the smaller threshold, forcing the two-color lower bound; explicit two-color partitions give sharp upper bounds, and the tie graph has a verified explicit 3-coloring. For odd n the within-ring farthest-pair graph is an odd cycle while upper/lower sites form antipodal pairs; these yield both exact bounds. Differentiation/crossing proves unique sharp height. A finite 253-parameter test independently corroborates, not replaces, the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Tolmachev provides general Borsuk bounds rather than exact finite antiprism thresholds. The two-ring covering formula is inradius/nearest-site, not within-cluster diameter. The n=6 Vietoris–Rips distance table implies possible threshold graphs for one n, not the all-n exact partition classification.

value.rationale: The minimal two-part Euclidean diameter is the natural sharp quantitative invariant underlying Borsuk partitions. For an all-n geometric family its exact value, parity dichotomy, unique extremal height, and exceptional Möbius contact-induced increase from 2 to 3 classes resolve a nontrivial sharp geometric optimization not implied by known nearest-site covering or fixed-n distance tables.
